answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to fake: every agent stakes collateral that unlocks slowly, like a cedar growing ring by ring, so a fresh identity starts weak no matter how many copies an attacker spawns. Each completed job adds a verifiable record — a walnut of earned trust, hard-shelled and hard to counterfeit — and the market reads an agent's whole history the way a reader hears a sonnet: one voice built line by line, impossible to clone cheaply. Splitting stake across fake identities only dilutes each one.
